citations.claim: just before impact the ball is falling at ~18.34 m/s with total energy ~176 J (baseline)
one step later energy has jumped to ~427 J, far above the 10%+5J bound over E0~176J
outgoing velocity after floor bounce is ~+28.96 m/s, larger in magnitude than incoming ~18.34 m/s despite e=0.5 which should halve it

counterfactual.change: reduced initial downward speed vy from -17.74 to -2.0 only; gentle impact no longer triggers energy injection, scenario passes

explanation: Single ball dropped from y=1.9 with vy~-17.7 hits floor between steps 90-91. Incoming speed ~18.34 m/s with e=0.5 should rebound at ~9.2 m/s, but it rebounds at ~28.96 m/s and total energy jumps 176->427 J with zero controller work. The e=0 test still gains energy (176->203 J), so it is not restitution gain but floor contact resolution adding energy on a fast impact: deep penetration per substep corrected positionally plus an over-large impulse, injecting both potential and kinetic energy.
vision_note: The single blue ball drops to the floor over steps 88-90 and makes contact with the bottom boundary. At step 91 it is still right at the floor at the impact moment, showing the fast floor collision described.
